title: Incremental response telemetry spec and developer checklist
summary: Draft spec and checklist for making incremental (streaming) responses first-class with telemetry that developers can use to debug fidelity degradations and tool-call reliability. Focus is on a small, opt-in server-driven framing (progress frames) plus SDK-level ergonomics for async iteration, resumability, and lightweight tool call confirmation semantics.
background: We have many ad hoc streaming behaviours across SDKs and server implementations. Customers building complex toolchains or mobile clients struggle to reason about partial outputs, tool call confirmations, and where quality regressions happen. This doc proposes a telemetry-forward incremental response contract and a practical developer checklist for SDK authors and product owners.
problem_statement: Observed gaps: (1) telemetry lacks token/frame-level signals tying latency/cost to semantic events (e.g., tool-call start/commit), (2) SDKs hide important state transitions (resumes, falls back to full-response) making debugging hard, (3) structured output + partial frames create ambiguous contracts for downstream connectors.
objectives: Define a compact incremental response frame model usable by hosted-api that surfaces: progress milestones, tool-call lifecycle events, schema-validated partial payloads.
Specify telemetry events and minimal tagging to trace token-level cost, latency, and fidelity across model variants and fallbacks.
Provide a developer-facing SDK checklist and async iterator patterns for safe resumable streams, idempotent tool invocation, and client-friendly error handling.
Keep opt-in compatibility: default behaviour unchanged; new frames are an additive metadata layer that clients can opt into via Accept headers or request flags.
success_metrics: Reduce mean time to diagnose tool-call failures from customer support by 60% within quarter after launch
Decrease incidence of silent schema regressions observed in production evaluations by 40% (measured by nightly eval divergence alerts),
Increase adoption of streaming SDK patterns for resumability by 30% among active integration customers in 90 days
requirements: R1: Frame envelope: every incremental message may include a frame header (0..n bytes) with: frame_id, seq, type (progress|token|tool_event|checkpoint|error), model_version, cost_estimate_usd (optional).
R2: Tool-call lifecycle events: explicit tool_event frames with phases {request, resolved, failed, cancelled} and a stable tool_call_id that is globally unique per session for tracing.

R3: Schema-validated partial payloads: support content-types application/json+partial and application/json+final. Partial payloads must include an explicit \"partial_path\" pointer where the fragment merges into the final JSON tree.
R4: Telemetry hooks: emit traceable events for frame_sent, frame_received (client), kv_cache_hit/miss, batching_delay_ms, tool_call_latency_ms, and model_fallback (with cause).
R5: Backwards compatibility: server must support a flag (X-Redwood-Incremental: true) and fall back to legacy streaming if client does not opt in.

R6: SDK ergonomics: provide an async iterator abstraction with explicit resume(token) API; SDK must expose event hooks for onFrame, onToolEvent, onCheckpoint, onResumeAttempt, onResumeSuccess, onResumeFailure.
R7: Security: tool_call_id and frame headers must not leak PII; any user identifiers must be hashed or removed before emission to telemetry streams available to multi-tenant dashboards.
api_contract_examples:
Example request header to opt-in: POST /v1/streams?model=redwood-small
Headers: Accept: text/event-stream, X-Redwood-Incremental: true, Prefer: return=partial, X-Client-Version: 1.4.2
Error frame pattern: { "frame_id": "f-err", "type": "error", "code": "TOOL_TIMEOUT", "message": "calendar.create timed out after 5s", "related_tool_call_id": "tc-789" }
sdk_patterns: Async iterator pattern (JS): for await (const frame of client.stream(...)) { if (frame.type === 'token') render(frame.text); else if (frame.type === 'tool_event') handleToolEvent(frame); }
Resume API: const resumeToken = await client.stream(...).checkpoint(); // persist locally. Later: client.resume(streamId, resumeToken)

Idempotent tool calls: SDK should surface a tool_call_id the client can provide on replays so server can dedupe; default SDK behaviour will auto-generate v4 UUIDs unless caller supplies an idempotency key.
Lightweight mobile pattern: expose a compact 'snapshot' for low-bandwidth clients (checkpointSummary) that contains only schema paths and hashes so client can reconcile without full payload transfer.
Polling vs streaming fallback: SDKs should offer .fetchFinal() that attempts a non-stream fallback when network conditions degrade or resume attempts fail after N retries.
telemetry_spec: Event taxonomy: TRACE_FRAME_SENT, TRACE_FRAME_RECV, TRACE_TOOL_EVENT, TRACE_CHECKPOINT_COMMIT, TRACE_RESUME_ATTEMPT, TRACE_RESUME_RESULT, TRACE_FALLBACK_INVOKED.
Minimum fields for all events: event_id, timestamp_iso, org_id_hashed, project_id, session_id, stream_id, model_version, frame_id (if applicable), cost_tokens, latency_ms.

Sampling policy: full sampling for tool_event frames for first 30 seconds of a new session, then 1% sampling for long-running sessions unless an error occurs (error forces full sampling for that session).
Tracing: correlate trace_id across client headers (X-Redwood-Trace) and server spans; include upstream (client SDK) and downstream (tool backend) spans in a single trace for tool_event sequences.
Alerting hooks: emit anomaly signal when model_fallback rate > 2% across requests for a model-version in 1h window or when average tool_call_latency_ms > 1s for a customer tier with SLO 500ms.
rollout_and_migration: Phase 0: internal preview — enable flag for internal accounts and Redwood partners; SDK experimental flags exposed in 1.4.x prerelease.
Phase 1: limited external beta — opt-in by project; provide migration checklist and SDK template; collect telemetry and run 2 week safety/eval sweep for schema regressions.
Phase 2: gradual default opt-in — enable for free-tier customers behind feature toggle; monitor success metrics and error rates, then flip opt-in to default for new sessions if stable.
Migration checklist for customers: ensure tool backends idempotency for repeated tool_call_id, add metric integration for TRACE_TOOL_EVENT, test resume flow under simulated mobile connectivity loss.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: telemetry volume explosion from full-token sampling. Mitigation: sample aggressively after warmup and cap retained traces per org per day; provide a diagnostic mode for customers to temporarily raise sampling.
Risk: clients misinterpret partial schemas and apply merges incorrectly. Mitigation: provide a reference merge utility in SDKs and clear doc examples for partial_path semantics.
Risk: tool_call_id leakage exposes internal ids. Mitigation: enforce server-side redaction and provide hashed ids in external telemetry streams; warn customers in migration guide.
Risk: increased latency due to per-frame headers. Mitigation: keep frame header compact (<= 128 bytes typical); allow a compact binary framing for high-throughput internal paths.
open_questions: Should cost_estimate_usd be populated in real-time per frame or only on checkpoints to avoid noise?
Do we need a separate 'fidelity_score' metric attached to checkpoints to reason about quality drift (and how to compute it cheaply at inference time)?
What's the recommended TTL for resume tokens and how long should server retain partial session state for resumability?
Should we allow configurable encryption for frame-level telemetry for enterprise private deployments?
